title: [Flight] Avoid main-thread stalls from large debug strings

posted.message: The replay expectation assumes the placeholder replaces only the second argument to `console.log`, but the implementation change is in `renderDebugModel` and may affect how the entire debug value is encoded/decoded. Can you confirm that replay still preserves the original argument count and ordering for multi-arg console calls, especially if one argument is omitted while others are retained? If not, this test could pass while masking a client-side formatting regression.

title: [19.0.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`

posted.message: `field` events are now queued onto the current `tail` file whenever any file is in flight. If payload order is `file A -> file B -> field for A`, that field will be attached to B instead of A, so the decoded FormData can still come out of order or lose the original grouping when multiple files are buffered concurrently. Consider tracking the file that was current when the field arrived, rather than always using the latest tail.

`bodyFinished` is only set from Busboy's `finish` event. If a file stream emits `error` or `busboyStream.destroy(error)` aborts parsing before `finish`, `close(response)` is never called from this path and the reply promise can hang unless the error path closes it elsewhere. Please verify the error handler always resolves or rejects the pending reply.

title: [19.1.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`

posted.message: `busboyStream.on('finish')` assumes every file has already fired `'end'`, but if a file stream is paused/backpressured or an error path delays completion, `flush()` can return early and this reports a global error instead of closing cleanly. Could this close be deferred until all pending files are drained rather than treating the invariant as fatal?

Fields are queued only while `tail !== null`, but once the head file completes and `flush()` advances, a text field arriving before the next file's `'file'` event will resolve immediately even though a later file may already be part of the same multipart ordering. That can reintroduce the ordering bug this patch is trying to fix. Consider tracking whether any pending file is still unflushed rather than just whether `tail` exists.

These tests validate the no-drop behavior for a very specific interleaving, but do not cover the case where a text field arrives after one file completes and before the next file event begins. Was that timing considered when changing from a global queue to per-file queues?

title: [19.2.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`

posted.message: `finish` now relies on every pending file eventually calling `end`, but if a file stream emits an error after `finish` has been observed, `closed` stays false and the code reports a synthetic 'incomplete file part' error in addition to the underlying stream error. Could this double-report or mask the real failure path? Consider guarding `finish` handling after any busboy/file error or centralizing terminal-state handling.

Queued text fields are only flushed when the head file completes. If busboy ever emits a `field` after a later file has already completed but before the earlier head file ends, that field is attached to the tail file and delayed until the head finishes. That preserves payload order, but it also means a failure in the head file can now drop unrelated later fields that were already fully parsed. Please verify this is intended; otherwise fields may be lost on partial file failures.

title: [19.0.x] Enable CI

posted.message: `ServerReferenceId` was changed from an opaque type to a plain string type. Was this intentional for this fork? Making it a regular `string` removes the nominal distinction that prevents accidentally passing arbitrary strings where a server reference ID is expected, which can hide bugs in the Flight client/server protocol. If the runtime truly only ever treats it as a string, consider keeping an opaque wrapper on the public boundary and only unwrapping internally.

title: [19.1.x] Enable CI

posted.message: This entry point now only exports `unstable_prerenderToNodeStream`, dropping the previously public `prerender` and `prerenderToNodeStream` symbols. Any existing Node consumers importing those names will start failing at runtime with `undefined` exports. If the API is meant to stay backward compatible, re-export the old names as aliases or keep the previous exports in addition to the unstable one.

`ServerReferenceId` changed from an opaque type to a plain `string`. That removes Flow's nominal boundary and makes it easier to accidentally pass arbitrary strings where a server reference ID is expected. Was the opacity intentionally dropped for this fork, or should this stay opaque to preserve type-safety across the client/server boundary?

title: ♻️ Do not accept underscore headers when using `convert_underscores=True` (the default)

posted.message: `processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))` is now applied for every parameter type handled by `request_params_to_args`, not just headers. If this helper is reused for query/cookie params, or if a field’s validation alias differs from the received key shape, this can incorrectly suppress 'extra' detection for unrelated inputs. Consider restricting this extra processed-key entry to header parameters only, or gating it on `convert_underscores` being active.

📝 Add docs references to central contributing docs

posted.message: `translations.md` is now treated as one of the core docs. If this file does not exist under `docs/` (or is generated later than the other docs), `scripts/docs.py` may fail or start reporting a missing-docs error. Could you confirm the file is present and intended to be part of the required set?

title: 🔧 Migrate docs from MkDocs to Zensical

posted.message: `is_non_translated_path()` now checks `path.as_posix().startswith(section)`, but `non_translated_sections` contains `reference{os.sep}`. On POSIX this yields `reference/`, which is fine, but on Windows `as_posix()` always uses `/` while `section` may contain `\`, so untranslated reference pages will be treated as translatable. Consider normalizing both sides to POSIX-style separators before comparing.

The new untranslated-page check only skips files under `reference/` and a few specific markdown files. The old hook also preserved other non-translated assets via MkDocs' file resolution. Because the staging step now copies the English tree and only overlays translated markdown, any untranslated non-markdown assets under language-specific docs will silently fall back to English without the previous explicit handling. If that is intentional, fine; otherwise it may break localized asset paths.

`live()` no longer accepts a language argument and always serves `en/docs`. This changes the behavior from previewing translated docs to English-only preview, which makes it impossible to verify non-English output locally via the documented command. If translated preview is still needed, consider keeping the `lang` parameter and pointing Zensical at the selected language stage.

title: Remove the use of Optional from Data Neo4j repository examples
Remove unnecessary null check

posted.message: `getProperties().getLettuce()` is dereferenced unconditionally here, but `RedisProperties#getLettuce()` is not proven non-null by the diff. If a user has no `spring.redis.lettuce.*` configuration, this will now throw a `NullPointerException` during bean creation. Please keep the null guard or ensure the property is initialized defensively.

title: Layer written outside the output location of '//' exception is thrown when using extract layers in root directory

posted.message: `outputRoot.relativize(layerDirectory)` can produce an empty path component when `layerDirectory` is created under a temp dir on a filesystem with a different root representation, which would make `layerName` empty or unexpected. Since the test later uses this value as both the iterator result and the expected layer name, it may not actually validate the intended root-destination case reliably. Consider hardcoding a simple relative layer name (for example, `dependencies`) and keeping only `outputRoot` as the destination under test.

title: Docker Compose support does not restore thread interrupt flag when catching InterruptedException
Use new Maven Resolver API for ModifiedClassPathClassLoader

posted.message: `RepositorySystemSupplier` may return a `RepositorySystem` implementation that does not expose `shutdown()`. If so, this call will fail at runtime or silently be ineffective depending on the API version. Could you confirm the supplier’s returned type and whether `shutdown()` is guaranteed here? If not, the safe pattern is to guard this call or avoid assuming lifecycle management on the `RepositorySystem` interface.

Creating a new `RepositorySystem` for every `resolveCoordinates` call may be expensive, since this code can run repeatedly while scanning annotations. If this method is called often, consider caching/reusing the resolver instance instead of constructing and tearing it down each time.

title: RabbitProperties enables SSL even when spring.rabbitmq.ssl.bundle is overridden to an empty string

posted.message: `determineEnabled()` now uses `StringUtils.hasText(this.bundle)` for the top-level SSL config, but the PR description says the same empty-string handling should also apply to `RabbitProperties.Stream.Ssl`. Could you confirm that the nested stream SSL path is updated as well, or is it intentionally handled elsewhere?

title: fix(http): preserve TLS options for proxy tunnels

posted.message: The wrapper replaces `agent.callback` with a function that always merges `userHttpsAgent.options` into the callback opts. If a future `HttpsProxyAgent` version changes the callback contract or relies on instance state captured by the original method, this monkey-patch could break tunneling behavior. Consider using the agent's documented extension points (or storing a custom callback when constructing the agent) instead of mutating the instance after creation.

title: fix: AxiosHeaders `toJSON()` return types

posted.message: Could you confirm whether `toJSON()` without arguments can ever return array-valued header entries at runtime? The new signature allows `Record<string, string | string[]>` when `asStrings` is omitted, but if the default behavior always serializes to strings this broader type may weaken consumers’ type safety unnecessarily.

title: fix(http): preserve basic auth on same-origin redirects (#6929)

posted.message: Comparing `new URL(redirectOptions.href).origin` to `parsed.origin` is stricter than the existing same-origin checks in Axios/follow-redirects in some edge cases. Redirects that are effectively same-origin but arrive with an equivalent hostname form (for example `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`, or other URL-normalization differences) will still drop credentials, which may reintroduce 401s for valid same-origin flows. If that is intentional, could you document it; otherwise consider reusing the same-origin logic already used elsewhere in the adapter.

title: Clean up error handling, fix a proto-pollution gap, and seal a few loose ends

posted.message: `own('params')` / `own('paramsSerializer')` look like presence checks, not the actual config values. As written, `buildURL()` will no longer receive the caller-provided params or serializer, so normal query-string serialization appears broken. Please pass the property values guarded by the `own()` check instead of the check result itself.

posted.message: Should inherited `socketPath` values be ignored only for security hardening, or is there any supported configuration path that still depends on prototype-derived values? This change intentionally blocks them, but it is a behavior change worth documenting for users relying on shared config objects or prototype-based defaults.
